label: prf:frobenius-pairing-unique
title: Proof of uniqueness of the Frobenius pairing
html:
Proof. Proof of uniqueness of the Frobenius pairing

Uniqueness reduces to the one-dimensionality of the relevant Hom-space: when A is simple, a Schur-type argument forces a one-dimensional space of forms, so any two Frobenius forms must agree up to a unit scalar. Concretely, each non-degenerate \int_A^{(i)} \colon A \to \mathbf{1} factors uniquely through the isomorphism A \xrightarrow{\sim} A^\vee as a morphism A^\vee \to \mathbf{1}. The space \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{C}}(A^\vee, \mathbf{1}) \cong \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{C}}(\mathbf{1}, A) \otimes \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{C}}(\mathbf{1}, A^\vee) is one-dimensional when A is simple (simple objects V). Hence any two Frobenius forms differ by a unit scalar c, and the composite \int_A^{(2)} \circ \mu = c \cdot \int_A^{(1)} \circ \mu inherits the same scaling.
